# Scope and main finding

This report reconstructs the **hypothetical trial in Table 2**, not the
paper's simulation tables. It uses the patient-level toxicity outcomes
printed in the paper and **computes the doses from the appendix rules**.
The expected doses are a separate reference file; they are never passed to
the decision engine.

The replay matches **all 45 dose assignments**, all 30 continuation Go
decisions, all 15 final exits, and the week-56 completion. It reproduces all
nine final dose/cycle count cells. There is one apparent typo among the
63 printed cumulative count cells: at week 40, cycle 3 D2, the patient rows
give **1/3**, whereas the printed total is **1/6**.

Three files contain the statistical functions: `R/mtpi2.R`, `R/basyc.R`, and
`R/mts.R`. The short helper file handles report formatting and independent
reference comparisons. The design code uses **base R only**. Knitting this
report needs `rmarkdown` and `knitr`.

Use the shared `phase1-dose-finding.Rproj` in the parent folder. This exercise
has no separate R project or render helper. From the shared project root,
run `rmarkdown::render("Lyu_2018/reproduce_table2.Rmd")` or
`source("Lyu_2018/validate.R")`; from this folder, use
`rmarkdown::render("reproduce_table2.Rmd")` or `source("validate.R")`.
All generated tables stay in this exercise's `results/` folder.

The primary source is Lyu, Curran and Ji (2018),
[DOI 10.1200/PO.18.00020](https://doi.org/10.1200/PO.18.00020):
Figure 2 on p. 5; Table 2 on pp. 6-8; appendix on pp. 16-18.

# The appendix rules in executable form

## Independent beta-binomial working models

Let $d$ index dose and $j$ index cycle. For each dose/cycle cell, accumulate
**all observed outcomes at that cell**, across cohorts:

$$
x_{dj}\mid n_{dj},p_{dj}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n_{dj},p_{dj}),
\qquad p_{dj}\sim\operatorname{Beta}(1,1),
$$

$$
p_{dj}\mid D\sim\operatorname{Beta}(1+x_{dj},1+n_{dj}-x_{dj}),
\qquad r_{dj}=\Pr(p_{dj}>p_T\mid D).
$$

These are working models for trial decisions. They do not fit a parametric
longitudinal toxicity or carryover model. The final sequence TPC calculation
is a separate step.

```{r settings}
settings <- basyc_settings(n_dose = 3, target = 0.30,
                           ei = c(0.25, 0.35), xi = 0.95)
settings
```

## The reusable mTPI-2 module

The equivalence interval is $(0.25,0.35)$. Split the lower and upper tails
into intervals of width 0.10, truncating only the intervals at 0 and 1.
For each interval $I$, compute

$$
\operatorname{UPM}(I)=\frac{\Pr(p\in I\mid x,n)}{|I|}.
$$

The interval with the largest UPM gives E (below the EI), S (in the EI), or
D (above the EI). The posterior overdose rule adds DU when $r>0.95$.
The code evaluates the **same small module separately at different
dose/cycle cells**. It never merges the current-cycle and next-cycle counts.

```{r mtpi2-examples}
mtpi2_intervals(settings$ei)

examples <- data.frame(x = c(0, 1, 3), n = c(3, 3, 6))
examples$decision <- mapply(mtpi2_decision, examples$x, examples$n,
                            MoreArgs = list(settings = settings))
knitr::kable(examples, caption = "Three mTPI-2 decisions used in the replay")

# Inspect every interval's posterior mass and UPM for 1 DLT in 3 patients.
knitr::kable(mtpi2_scores(1, 3, settings), digits = 5)
```

For zero observations the implementation returns S. Exact UPM ties prefer
D, then S, then E. These explicit conventions do not affect Table 2.

## Continuation and safety

For a cohort completing cycle $j<J$, DCR examines the lowest dose in the
**destination cycle**:

$$
\mathrm{DCR}(j)=
\begin{cases}
\mathrm{NG},&r_{1,j+1}>\xi,\\
\mathrm{G},&r_{1,j+1}\le\xi.
\end{cases}
$$

Patients exit after the last cycle. Additionally, the trial stops when any
cycle's lowest dose satisfies $r_{1j}>\xi$. If dose $d$ in cycle $j$ is unsafe,
exclude all $(d',j')$ with $d'\ge d$ and $j'\ge j$, permanently. Global trial
stopping takes precedence over further continuation or allocation.

## DAR-1, DAR-2a and DAR-2b

Write $T(d,j)$ for the candidate dose index returned by the cell-specific
mTPI-2 module, bounded to the available dose range.

- **Default:** cohort 1 receives D1 in every cycle, subject to continuation.
- **DAR-1:** a new cohort's cycle-1 dose is $T(d_{\mathrm{previous}},1)$,
  using the preceding cohort's cycle-1 dose and cumulative cell data.
- For an existing patient moving from $j$ to $j+1$, set $i_1=T(d,j)$.
  If the previous cohort used several doses in cycle $j+1$, calculate all
  their candidates and take

$$
i_2=\min_{u\in\{\text{previous cohort's doses in cycle }j+1\}}T(u,j+1).
$$

Then use the current patient's observed toxicity $Y$:

$$
d_{\mathrm{next}}=
\begin{cases}
\min(i_1,i_2),&Y=0\quad\text{(DAR-2a)},\\
\min\{\max(d-1,1),i_2\},&Y=1\quad\text{(DAR-2b)}.
\end{cases}
$$

Thus, after a DLT at D1, the patient can remain at D1 if continuation is
allowed. A DLT does not automatically remove an individual from all later
cycles: the motivating trial assumes washout and recovery.

`dar2()` handles each patient separately using the same rule. This preserves
the personalized split: patients sharing a dose and current outcome receive
the same decision. All distinct doses used by the previous cohort are
included in $i_2$ even when that cohort has split into subcohorts.

# Reconstruct Table 2 from outcomes

## Read only the toxicity inputs

The CSV codes O as 0 and X as 1. Dose paths are not in this input file.

```{r input}
input <- read.csv(lyu_path("data", "table2_outcomes.csv"))
knitr::kable(input, caption = "Patient-level outcomes transcribed from Table 2")
outcomes <- as.matrix(input[, c("y1", "y2", "y3")])
```

## Run the design

At each eight-week epoch, the engine observes **all outcomes due at that
time**, updates cumulative counts and safety, then makes allocation
decisions. It enrolls a new cohort after the preceding cohort finishes
cycle 1. The preceding cohort's destination-cycle outcomes are observed
before being used in DAR-2. No future outcome is used.

```{r replay}
fit <- run_basyc(outcomes, cohort_size = 3, cycle_weeks = 8,
                 settings = settings)
data.frame(Patients = fit$n_patient, Observed_patient_cycles = nrow(fit$observed),
           End_week = fit$end_week, Stopped_early = fit$stopped)
```

## Inspect the split at week 16

The cycle-1 D2 data are 1/3, giving candidate D2; the destination cycle-2
D1 data are 0/3, also giving candidate D2. Patients 5-6 therefore receive
D2. Patient 4 experienced a DLT, so DAR-2b lowers that patient's dose to D1.

```{r week16}
knitr::kable(subset(fit$assignments, week == 16 & cohort == 2,
                    select = c(patient, cycle, rule, current, i1, i2, dose)))
```

## Inspect the previous cohort's split at week 24

Cohort 2 used D1 and D2 in cycle 2. Both modules contribute to cohort 3's
destination-cycle candidate: D1 has 0/4 and suggests D2, but D2 has 1/2 and
suggests D1. Their minimum is D1. Current cycle-1 D2 also has 3/6 and
suggests D1. All three patients in cohort 3 receive D1 in cycle 2.

```{r week24}
knitr::kable(subset(fit$assignments, week == 24 & cohort == 3,
                    select = c(patient, rule, current, previous, i1, i2, dose)))
```

# Table 2, assessment by assessment

The following panels preserve the patient-level information in Table 2,
using a compact layout. **O/X at D# is observed; Assigned D# is a planned
next cycle whose outcome is not available yet.** Historical completed
patients are left as individual rows instead of being compressed with an
asterisk. The count rows contain observed patients only.

```{r weekly-panels, results='asis', echo=TRUE}
for (week in seq(8, 56, by = 8)) {
  cat("\n\n## Week ", week, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(table2_at_week(fit, week), format = "html",
                     table.attr = "class='table table-condensed'"))
  cat("\n\n")
  s <- fit$snapshots[[as.character(week)]]
  cells <- matrix(paste0(s$x, "/", s$n), nrow = settings$n_dose)
  count_table <- data.frame(Cycle = seq_len(fit$n_cycle), t(cells), check.names = FALSE)
  names(count_table)[-1] <- paste0("D", seq_len(settings$n_dose))
  print(knitr::kable(count_table, format = "html",
                     table.attr = "class='table table-condensed'",
                     caption = "Cumulative DLTs / observed patients"))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

At week 48, patients 13-15 have finished cycle 2 and are assigned cycle-3
doses D1, D2, D2. At week 56 their outcomes are X, X, O, respectively.
This changes cycle-3 D1 from 1/6 to 2/7 and D2 from 2/6 to 3/8.

# Final MTS: an explicit implementation of Appendix p. 18

## Sequence-specific data and posterior screening

Retain completed, actually used sequences that pass the posterior safety
screen. For sequence $s$, use only patients completing that sequence:

$$
\widetilde q_s=\frac{\sum_j x_{sj}}{\sum_j n_{sj}}.
$$

This differs from averaging the pooled dose/cycle empirical rates used
during allocation. The appendix's screen uses **any** unsafe cycle
($\exists j$), despite an inconsistent use of the word "each" in its prose.

```{r sequence-data}
knitr::kable(sequence_summary(fit), digits = 4)
```

## Orderings, PAVA and votes

Order by intensity $I(s)=\sum_jd_{sj}$. Enumerate all permutations within
each tied intensity group; for this dataset there are $2!\times3!=12$
complete orderings. Apply PAVA over **each full ordering**, including
violations between different intensities.

```{r pava-demo}
# A violation between positions 2 and 3 is pooled, without changing ranks.
pava(c(0.10, 0.30, 0.20, 0.40))
```

For each ordering $w$, select a sequence nearest to $p_T$. Count its
selection frequency over orderings. Only at the final vote stage restrict
to nonincreasing dose sequences, then choose the most frequent one. Final
frequency ties favor lower intensity, then lower first, second, ... dose.

The appendix does not fully specify **PAVA weights** or **nearest-target
ties inside an ordering**. Therefore these arguments are required, and we
show sensitivity rather than claiming a unique published MTS for Table 2.

```{r mts}
mts <- select_mts(fit, weights = "equal", nearest_tie = "lower")
knitr::kable(mts$per_order)
knitr::kable(mts$votes)
mts$recommendation
```

```{r mts-sensitivity}
choices <- expand.grid(weights = c("equal", "patient_cycles"),
                        nearest_tie = c("lower", "higher"),
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
choices$MTS <- mapply(function(w, t) {
  select_mts(fit, weights = w, nearest_tie = t)$recommendation
}, choices$weights, choices$nearest_tie)
knitr::kable(choices)
```

Here the within-ordering tie convention changes the recommendation from
(2,1,1) to (2,2,1). **Table 2 does not report a final MTS**, so these choices
cannot be adjudicated against a published Table 2 recommendation. If no
nonincreasing sequence receives a vote, the implementation returns no MTS
instead of silently introducing another fallback rule. Enumeration stops
with an informative error if it would exceed `max_orders`.


# Table 3: parallel simulation and comparison with the paper

## Functions and the one-file workflow

The Table 2 reproduction above stays unchanged. Table 3 scenarios 1-6 use the same
allocation and final-recommendation functions:

| Function | Called for |
|:--|:--|
| `simulate_table3()` in `simulate.R` | Repeating scenarios 1-6 in parallel batches |
| `run_basyc()` in `R/basyc.R` | Trial allocation, continuation and safety |
| `select_mts()` in `R/mts.R` | PAVA and final MTS selection in each trial |
| `summarize_table3()` in `simulate.R` | Summarizing the saved simulation data |
| `table3_reference()` in `simulate.R` | The transcribed published comparison values |

In a **local Mac terminal**, from the shared project folder, run:

```sh
bash unity.sh 10000 auto 2018
```

This uploads changed code, requests up to 32 currently available Slurm CPU
cores, and runs 10,000 trials **per scenario for scenarios 1-6** (60,000 total), downloads **`data/table3.rds`**, and renders **this same Rmd**.
The shell script requests a compute node, not computation on the login node.
Password/Duo entry is private and manual. Keep the terminal open until the
command finishes; do not upload new code while that job is running.

The simulation call performed on Unity is:

```{r table3-reproduction-call, eval=FALSE}
source("Lyu_2018/simulate.R")
result <- simulate_table3(nsim = 10000, cores = 32, seed = 2018, scenarios = 1:6)
saveRDS(result, "Lyu_2018/data/table3.rds")
```

The function uses `parallel::mclapply()` over batches of trials from scenarios 1-6. Every trial has its
own seed, so changing the number of workers does not change the simulated
trials. Workers never exceed `SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK`. The RDS holds trial records,
dose/cycle counts, completed patient sequences and settings together.
**Knitting reads this file; it does not rerun the simulation.**

## Scenario settings and conventions

There are three doses, three cycles, at most 15 patients and three patients
per cohort. The target is 0.30, EI is (0.25, 0.35), and the posterior safety
threshold is 0.95. For scenario-specific first-cycle probabilities,

$$
p_{dj}=\min\{1,p_{d1}(1.1)^{j-1}\},\qquad j=1,2,3.
$$

The probability cap is explicit: in scenario 4 the literal multiplier gives
$0.84(1.1)^2=1.0164$ for D3 in cycle 3, which is capped at one.

Independent patient/cycle uniforms generate binary toxicity at the dose actually assigned:

$$
Y_{ij}=\mathbf{1}\{U_{ij}<p_{d_{ij},j}\},\qquad
U_{ij}\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Uniform}(0,1).
$$

This independence assumption is not fully specified by the paper. PAVA weights,
nearest-target ties within an ordering, and the Figure 2/appendix safety
convention are recorded in the saved settings and remain explicit function
arguments. The Table 3 defaults use equal PAVA weights, the higher position
in a within-order nearest-target tie, and the appendix safety rule (minimum
sample size zero). The Table 2 section above demonstrates both tie choices.
The comparison below is a reproduction attempt, **not a claim that
all Table 3 numbers already agree**. Increasing simulation size cannot resolve
a different implementation convention.

```{r table3-read-data}
source(lyu_path("simulate.R"))  # Defines functions; does not launch a simulation.
table3_file <- lyu_path("data", "table3.rds")
has_table3 <- file.exists(table3_file)
if (has_table3) {
  table3 <- readRDS(table3_file)
  scenarios <- sort(unique(table3$trials$scenario))
  recorded_scenarios <- table3$settings$value[table3$settings$setting == "scenarios"]
  if (length(recorded_scenarios)) {
    expected <- sort(as.integer(strsplit(recorded_scenarios, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]))
    stopifnot(identical(scenarios, expected))
  }
  table3_summary <- summarize_table3(table3)
  published <- table3_reference()
  nsim <- as.integer(table3$settings$value[
    table3$settings$setting == "nsim_per_scenario"])
  stopifnot(nrow(table3$trials) == length(scenarios) * nsim,
            all(table(table3$trials$scenario) == nsim))
} else {
  cat("No saved Table 3 simulation yet. Run bash unity.sh 10000 auto 2018 locally.")
}
```

```{r table3-run-details, eval=has_table3, results='asis'}
cat("**Saved run:** ", nsim, " trials per scenario (", length(scenarios) * nsim,
    " total).\n\n", sep = "")
if (!is.null(table3$runtime_seconds)) {
  cat(sprintf("**Total simulation runtime:** %.2f minutes (%.2f seconds).\n\n",
              table3$runtime_seconds / 60, table3$runtime_seconds))
  cat("Runtime is wall-clock simulation time, excluding queueing and file transfers.\n\n")
}
if (!is.null(table3$slurm)) knitr::kable(table3$slurm, caption = "Verified server job and runtime")
if (nsim < 10000) cat("**Pilot only:** the paper used 10,000 trials per scenario.\n\n")
knitr::kable(table3$settings)
knitr::kable(subset(table3$truth, cycle == 1), digits = 3,
             caption = "Scenario truths in cycle 1 and the true MTS")
```

## Reading the completed comparison

The following compact table puts true-MTS selection and early termination
side by side. The remaining plots show the full sequence-level comparison.

```{r table3-summary-table, eval=has_table3}
true_targets <- vapply(lyu_scenarios(), lyu_true_mts, character(1))
overview <- do.call(rbind, lapply(scenarios, function(s) {
  target <- true_targets[s]
  paper <- subset(published$selection, scenario == s & sequence == target)
  sim <- subset(table3_summary$selection, scenario == s & sequence == target)
  data.frame(Scenario = s, True_MTS = target,
    Paper_correct_selection_pct = if (nrow(paper)) 100 * paper$selection else NA_real_,
    Sim_correct_selection_pct = 100 * sim$selection,
    Paper_early_stop_pct = 100 * published$early_stop$stopped_early[published$early_stop$scenario == s],
    Sim_early_stop_pct = 100 * table3_summary$early_stop$stopped_early[table3_summary$early_stop$scenario == s])
}))
knitr::kable(overview, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

In scenario 4, simulated "correct selection" means no MTS is recommended.
The paper does not report that exact probability separately from its early
termination probability, so its selection entry is left missing.

## True toxicity curves and the true MTS

The first plot follows the true toxicity of each fixed dose across cycles.
The bold black path follows the true MTS dose in each cycle. The target is
0.30 and the shaded EI is (0.25, 0.35). Scenario 4 has no safe MTS.

```{r table3-true-cycle-curves, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, echo=FALSE, fig.cap='True dose/cycle probabilities. Colored lines hold dose fixed; the black path follows the true MTS. Labels give its dose in each cycle.'}
truth_matrices <- lyu_scenarios()
true_mts <- vapply(truth_matrices, lyu_true_mts, character(1))
dose_colors <- c("#2471a3", "#229954", "#c0392b")
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (s in 1:6) {
  p <- truth_matrices[[s]]
  plot(1:3, rep(0, 3), type = "n", ylim = c(0, 1), xaxt = "n",
       xlab = "Treatment cycle", ylab = "True DLT probability",
       main = paste("Scenario", s, "| MTS", true_mts[s]))
  rect(.8, .25, 3.2, .35, col = "#edf2f4", border = NA)
  abline(h = .30, lty = 2, col = "#555555")
  axis(1, at = 1:3)
  for (d in 1:3) lines(1:3, p[d, ], type = "b", pch = 15 + d,
                       col = dose_colors[d], lwd = 1.5)
  if (true_mts[s] != "None") {
    doses <- as.integer(strsplit(true_mts[s], ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
    y <- p[cbind(doses, 1:3)]
    lines(1:3, y, type = "b", lwd = 3, col = "black", pch = 21, bg = "#f4d03f")
    text(1:3, y, paste0("D", doses), pos = 1, cex = .8)
  } else text(2, .15, "No safe MTS", col = "#c0392b")
  if (s == 1) legend("topleft", c("D1", "D2", "D3", "True MTS"),
                     col = c(dose_colors, "black"), lty = 1, cex = .7, bty = "n")
}
par(old_par)
```

For a nonincreasing sequence $s=(d_{s1},d_{s2},d_{s3})$, its true TPC is

$$
q_s=\frac{1}{3}\sum_{j=1}^3p_{d_{sj},j}.
$$

The next plot shows all ten nonincreasing candidate sequences against dose
intensity $I_s=\sum_jd_{sj}$. Small horizontal offsets separate sequences with
the same intensity; they do **not** impose a toxicity ordering. Blue points
satisfy $p_{d_{sj},j}<0.35$ in every cycle, red points fail that criterion, and
the gold point is the true MTS. A sequence can have TPC near 0.30 and still
contain an unsafe dose/cycle cell.

```{r table3-true-sequence-curves, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, echo=FALSE, fig.cap='True sequence TPC and safety. Gold marks the true MTS; scenario 4 has none. Sequence labels concatenate the three dose indices.'}
candidate_paths <- as.matrix(expand.grid(d1 = 1:3, d2 = 1:3, d3 = 1:3))
candidate_paths <- candidate_paths[apply(candidate_paths, 1, function(d) all(diff(d) <= 0)), ]
intensity <- rowSums(candidate_paths)
labels <- apply(candidate_paths, 1, paste, collapse = "")
keys <- apply(candidate_paths, 1, paste, collapse = ",")
offsets <- ave(intensity, intensity, FUN = function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 1) 0 else seq(-.13, .13, length.out = length(x))
})
text_positions <- ave(intensity, intensity, FUN = function(x) rep(c(3, 1), length.out = length(x)))
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (s in 1:6) {
  p <- truth_matrices[[s]]
  q <- apply(candidate_paths, 1, function(d) mean(p[cbind(d, 1:3)]))
  safe <- apply(candidate_paths, 1, function(d) all(p[cbind(d, 1:3)] < .35))
  plot(intensity, q, type = "n", xlim = c(2.6, 9.4), ylim = c(0, 1), yaxt = "n",
       xlab = "Sum of dose indices", ylab = "True sequence TPC",
       main = paste("Scenario", s))
  rect(2.6, .25, 9.4, .35, col = "#edf2f4", border = NA)
  axis(2, at = seq(0, 1, .2), las = 1)
  abline(h = .30, lty = 2, col = "#555555")
  points(intensity + offsets, q, pch = 21,
         bg = ifelse(safe, "#2471a3", "#e6a5a0"), col = "white", cex = 1.4)
  selected <- which(keys == true_mts[s])
  if (length(selected)) points(intensity[selected] + offsets[selected], q[selected],
                               pch = 23, bg = "#f4d03f", cex = 2)
  text(intensity + offsets, q, labels, pos = text_positions, cex = .65)
  if (s == 1) legend("topleft", c("Safe cells", "Unsafe cell", "True MTS"),
                     pch = c(21, 21, 23), pt.bg = c("#2471a3", "#e6a5a0", "#f4d03f"),
                     cex = .7, bty = "n")
  if (s == 4) text(6, .12, "All sequences contain unsafe doses", col = "#c0392b", cex = .8)
}
par(old_par)
```

Scenarios 1-2 have a moderately toxic lowest dose and only 15 patients, so
early DLTs can limit exploration before the final recommendation. Scenario 3
has safe upper doses and permits escalation to (3,3,3). Scenario 4 tests the
ability to stop, rather than successful selection of a safe sequence. In
scenario 5 the D2-to-D3 toxicity jump leaves (2,2,2) as the highest safe path,
even though its TPC is below the EI; scenario 6 leaves only (1,1,1) safe.
These are explanations from the truth settings, not guarantees of selection
performance. The simulation plots below show the actual operating behavior.

## MTS selection and completed-sequence outcomes

For each published sequence, the selection probability and its Monte Carlo
standard error are

$$
\widehat\pi_s=\frac{1}{B}\sum_{b=1}^B\mathbf{1}\{\widehat s_b=s\},
\qquad \operatorname{MCSE}(\widehat\pi_s)
=\sqrt{\widehat\pi_s(1-\widehat\pi_s)/B}.
$$

The mean and SD of DLTs below are calculated across completed patients with
that actual sequence. Sequence allocation is their number divided by $15B$;
patients with incomplete sequences are not assigned a completed sequence.
These interpretations of the printed columns are stated explicitly for review.
Selection/allocation numbers such as 0.190 are **proportions** (19.0%).

```{r table3-sequence-comparison, eval=has_table3}
comparison <- merge(published$selection, table3_summary$selection,
                    by = c("scenario", "sequence"), suffixes = c("_paper", "_sim"))
sequence_table <- with(comparison, data.frame(
  Scenario = scenario, Sequence = sequence,
  Paper_Pr = selection_paper, Sim_Pr = selection_sim,
  Difference = selection_sim - selection_paper, MCSE = mcse,
  Paper_DLT = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", mean_dlts_paper, sd_dlts_paper),
  Sim_DLT = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f)", mean_dlts_sim, sd_dlts_sim),
  Paper_allocation = allocation_paper, Sim_allocation = allocation_sim))
knitr::kable(sequence_table, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r table3-agreement, eval=has_table3, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
combined_mcse <- with(comparison, sqrt(selection_sim * (1-selection_sim) / nsim +
                                        selection_paper * (1-selection_paper) / 10000))
valid <- is.finite(comparison$selection_paper) & is.finite(comparison$selection_sim)
cat(sprintf("Largest absolute selection difference: **%.2f percentage points**. ",
            100 * max(abs(comparison$selection_sim[valid] - comparison$selection_paper[valid]))))
cat(sum(abs(comparison$selection_sim[valid] - comparison$selection_paper[valid]) > 3 * combined_mcse[valid]),
    "of", sum(valid), "published selection entries differ by more than three combined Monte Carlo standard errors.\n")
```


Only the paper's printed sequence rows for scenarios 1-6 are compared above; all simulated
sequences and "None" are available in `table3_summary$selection`.

## Dose/cycle counts and early termination

Dose/cycle counts average over **all trials**, including early stops.

```{r table3-cell-comparison, eval=has_table3}
cell_comparison <- merge(published$cells, table3_summary$cells,
                         by = c("scenario", "dose", "cycle"),
                         suffixes = c("_paper", "_sim"))
cell_table <- with(cell_comparison, data.frame(
  Scenario = scenario, Dose = dose, Cycle = cycle,
  Paper_DLT_of_N = sprintf("%.3f of %.3f", dlts_paper, n_paper),
  Sim_DLT_of_N = sprintf("%.3f of %.3f", dlts_sim, n_sim)))
knitr::kable(cell_table, row.names = FALSE)

stop_comparison <- merge(published$early_stop, table3_summary$early_stop,
                         by = "scenario", suffixes = c("_paper", "_sim"))
stop_comparison[-1] <- 100 * stop_comparison[-1]
knitr::kable(stop_comparison, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Early termination (%)")
```

## Graphical comparison with the paper

The bars compare selection of the true MTS in scenarios with a safe MTS,
and early stopping in all scenarios. Scenario 4 has no safe MTS and is
therefore assessed by early stopping rather than by a reported true-MTS
selection probability. Error bars show simulation Monte Carlo uncertainty.

```{r table3-key-metric-plots, eval=has_table3, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.5, echo=FALSE, fig.cap='Published versus simulated operating characteristics. Error bars are 95% Monte Carlo intervals for the simulation; they do not include uncertainty in the paper estimates.'}
correct <- do.call(rbind, lapply(scenarios, function(s) {
  target <- true_mts[s]
  if (target == "None") return(NULL)
  paper <- subset(published$selection, scenario == s & sequence == target)
  sim <- subset(table3_summary$selection, scenario == s & sequence == target)
  data.frame(scenario = s, paper = paper$selection, sim = sim$selection, se = sim$mcse)
}))
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
colors <- c("#95a5a6", "#2471a3")
values <- rbind(correct$paper, correct$sim)
x <- barplot(values, beside = TRUE, col = colors, names.arg = paste0("S", correct$scenario),
             ylim = c(0, min(1, max(values + .1))), ylab = "Probability",
             main = "Selection of the true MTS", border = NA)
nz <- correct$se > 0
arrows(x[2, nz], pmax(0, correct$sim[nz] - 1.96 * correct$se[nz]),
       x[2, nz], pmin(1, correct$sim[nz] + 1.96 * correct$se[nz]), angle = 90, code = 3, length = .04)
legend("topright", c("Paper", "Simulation"), fill = colors, bty = "n", cex = .8)
values <- rbind(stop_comparison$stopped_early_paper, stop_comparison$stopped_early_sim)
x <- barplot(values, beside = TRUE, col = colors,
             names.arg = paste0("S", stop_comparison$scenario), ylim = c(0, 105),
             ylab = "Early termination (%)", main = "Stopping for excessive toxicity", border = NA)
p <- stop_comparison$stopped_early_sim / 100
se <- 100 * sqrt(p * (1-p) / nsim)
nz <- se > 0
arrows(x[2, nz], pmax(0, values[2, nz] - 1.96 * se[nz]),
       x[2, nz], pmin(100, values[2, nz] + 1.96 * se[nz]), angle = 90, code = 3, length = .04)
legend("topleft", c("Paper", "Simulation"), fill = colors, bty = "n", cex = .8)
text(x, values, sprintf("%.2f", values), pos = 3, cex = .65)
par(old_par)
```

The next plots compare **every numerically reported sequence-selection
probability**, not just selection of the true MTS. Agreement would place
points near the diagonal. Labels identify the true MTS and the two largest
selection discrepancies within a scenario;
the gold point marks the true MTS when it appears among the printed rows.

```{r table3-all-selection-plots, eval=has_table3, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, echo=FALSE, fig.cap='Selection probabilities from the paper and simulation. The diagonal indicates agreement. Vertical intervals show 95% simulation Monte Carlo uncertainty.'}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (s in scenarios) {
  z <- subset(comparison, scenario == s & is.finite(selection_paper))
  limit <- max(.1, z$selection_paper, z$selection_sim + 1.96 * z$mcse) * 1.15
  plot(z$selection_paper, z$selection_sim, xlim = c(0, limit), ylim = c(0, limit),
       xlab = "Paper selection probability", ylab = "Simulation selection probability",
       main = paste("Scenario", s), pch = 21,
       bg = ifelse(z$sequence == true_mts[s], "#f4d03f", "#2471a3"))
  abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "#777777")
  nz <- z$mcse > 0
  arrows(z$selection_paper[nz], pmax(0, z$selection_sim[nz] - 1.96 * z$mcse[nz]),
         z$selection_paper[nz], z$selection_sim[nz] + 1.96 * z$mcse[nz],
         angle = 90, code = 3, length = .03, col = "#2471a3")
  label <- unique(c(which(z$sequence == true_mts[s]),
                     head(order(abs(z$selection_sim - z$selection_paper), decreasing = TRUE), 2)))
  text(z$selection_paper[label], z$selection_sim[label], gsub(",", "", z$sequence[label]), pos = 4, cex = .65)
}
par(old_par)
```

Finally, dose/cycle allocation can agree even when final MTS selection differs.
This comparison helps separate the trial-allocation engine from the final
PAVA/voting convention. Each point is one dose/cycle cell.

```{r table3-allocation-plots, eval=has_table3, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, echo=FALSE, fig.cap='Mean patient allocation per dose/cycle cell, averaged over all trials. The diagonal indicates agreement with Table 3.'}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (s in scenarios) {
  z <- subset(cell_comparison, scenario == s)
  limit <- max(1, z$n_paper, z$n_sim) * 1.12
  plot(z$n_paper, z$n_sim, xlim = c(0, limit), ylim = c(0, limit),
       xlab = "Paper mean patients", ylab = "Simulation mean patients",
       main = paste("Scenario", s), pch = 19, col = dose_colors[z$dose])
  abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "#777777")
  label <- z$n_paper > .2 | z$n_sim > .2
  text(z$n_paper[label], z$n_sim[label], paste0("D", z$dose[label], "C", z$cycle[label]), pos = 4, cex = .6)
}
par(old_par)
```

## Remaining discrepancies

```{r table3-final-diagnostics, eval=has_table3, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
allocation_rmse <- sqrt(mean((cell_comparison$n_sim - cell_comparison$n_paper)^2))
cat(sprintf("Mean dose/cycle allocation RMSE versus the paper: **%.3f patients per cell**.\n\n", allocation_rmse))
if (any(abs(comparison$selection_sim[valid] - comparison$selection_paper[valid]) > 3 * combined_mcse[valid])) {
  cat("**This run does not fully reproduce Table 3 numerically.** Some sequence-selection discrepancies exceed Monte Carlo uncertainty. ",
      "PAVA/tie handling, safety conventions and the outcome generator need further review; this comparison does not identify their individual contributions.\n\n")
}
no_mts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(scenarios, function(s) {
  z <- subset(table3$trials, scenario == s)
  data.frame(Scenario = s, No_MTS_pct = 100 * mean(z$selected_mts == "None"),
              Early_stop_pct = 100 * mean(z$stopped_early),
              No_MTS_without_early_stop_pct = 100 * mean(z$selected_mts == "None" & !z$stopped_early))
}))
knitr::kable(no_mts, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Diagnostic: no recommendation versus an early-stopped trial")
```

A completed trial can return no MTS under the implemented final-vote rule
when no nonincreasing sequence receives a vote. These cases are distinct
from safety stopping. The table above exposes their frequency so that this
implementation convention can be reviewed explicitly.

The paper's column "patients treated above MTS" is not reconstructed here:
the article does not give an explicit cross-cycle counting rule for that
percentage. The dose/cycle counts are provided for direct checking; a new
exposure definition should not silently be presented as the paper's definition.
